planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring once frost danger has passed, in fast-draining soil or a succulent mix.

directions: Safari Rose is a dwarf, patented aloe hybrid (PP28002) bred for compact clumping growth and an unusually long bloom season, pushing up spikes of rose-pink flowers from summer into winter even in its first year. It thrives in full sun to light afternoon shade with excellent drainage, needing only occasional watering once roots are established. The thick, spiny-edged rosettes stay evergreen and resist deer, making it a reliable choice for rock gardens, edging, and mixed succulent containers in zones 9a-11b. No pruning is required beyond removing spent flower stalks.

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in a bright but sheltered, partly shaded bed or container with consistently moist, well-drained soil.

directions: Sterling Moon (PP33164) is part of the Lunar Lights series, grown for its puckered green leaves flecked with silvery mint and new growth tinged pink, topped by salmon-pink flowers from spring through fall. It performs best in a bright, partly shaded spot with consistent moisture and benefits from regular feeding during the growing season. The mounding, deciduous perennial dies back in winter in its hardiness range (zones 7a-9b) and returns from the roots each spring. Use it in shaded borders, mass plantings, or containers where its foliage color can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in full sun with good drainage, giving it room for its narrow, upright growth habit.

directions: Butterfly Towers Magenta ('Tobud1305') is a columnar butterfly bush bred to send up narrow, upright spikes of magenta flowers rather than the typical arching sprays of older buddleia varieties. Give it full sun for the strongest bloom and moderate water; it tolerates heat and drought well once established. Because it blooms on new wood, cut the stems back hard in late winter to keep the vertical habit tight and encourage fresh flowering growth. Its narrow 2-3 foot width makes it useful as a hedge, screen, or vertical accent in zones 5a-10b.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in full sun with good drainage; its narrow, pyramidal form suits tight planting beds.

directions: Butterfly Towers White ('TMBU08/3', PP35051) shares the same narrow, upright growth habit as its magenta counterpart in the series but produces towering spikes of white flowers that draw butterflies all summer. It wants full sun and moderate water, and like other buddleias it should be cut back hard in early spring to renew its columnar form. The deciduous shrub dies back to the ground in colder parts of its range (zones 5a-10b) and rebounds reliably each year. Its compact 2-3 foot spread suits narrow beds, screens, and cutting gardens.

planting.note: Plant in part sun in a hole about three times the width of the root ball; backfill, water in, and mulch lightly.

directions: Ever Sky Light is a repeat-blooming agapanthus hybrid that sends up dark blue flower clusters on sturdy stalks from spring into summer, then continues flowering intermittently if spent stalks are removed. It prefers part sun and, once established, needs little supplemental water thanks to its drought tolerance. The clumping evergreen foliage stays tidy without pruning and resists deer, making this a good fit for poolside beds, containers, and mass plantings in zones 8a-11b. Deadhead spent flower stalks regularly to extend the bloom window.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun to part shade with light, well-drained soil; its cascading habit suits raised containers and basket edges.

directions: Design-A-Line (ROMA06, PP24764) is a dwarf cordyline hybrid with a cascading, trailing habit and leaves that hold a rich burgundy color all year rather than fading with the seasons. Grow it in full sun to part shade with light, infrequent watering; it is hardy to roughly 10-20 degrees F in zones 8a-11b. Its compact 3-foot mound and spilling form make it well suited to container edges, hanging baskets, and pairings with succulents. It needs essentially no pruning to maintain its shape.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; the compact tufts need no cutting back to stay neat.

directions: Beyond Blue ('Casca11', PP23307) is a compact ornamental fescue selected for intensely powder-blue blades that hold their color through the growing season without browning out. Plant it in full sun with moderate water in well-drained soil; the tight, mounding tufts stay evergreen and need no cutting back. Hardy to roughly -30 to -20 degrees F across zones 4a-8b, it tolerates both heat and cold well once established. Use it for edging, small-space borders, containers, or massed on slopes for erosion control.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun to considerable shade with well-drained soil; established clumps tolerate extended dry spells.

directions: Platinum Beauty ('Roma 13', PP25962) is a variegated lomandra selection with arching, strap-like blades striped in green and creamy platinum that provide color year-round. It handles full sun or considerable shade and, once rooted in, needs only occasional watering thanks to its drought tolerance. Clumping and evergreen, it sends up creamy flower spikes from autumn into spring and never needs shearing to stay neat. Its fine texture and erosion-controlling roots make it useful on slopes, in mass plantings, or as a border grass in zones 8a-10b.
